entries.name: Harness kit: one set-up that holds a second person's sessions to the method
entries.what: The set-up builds seven Rust programs and wires six of them as hooks into a project's own settings (the clone or a repository of hers): the start hook that loads the short rules, the window ceiling, the model by kind of job, the count of helpers at once, token limits with a basis and a cap, and the limit on review rounds. With it: the short rules, the README, the parallel commands for any repository (units in their own copies landing through the check in one order, test files side by side), a counter of what each helper cost, the clean-clone check, and the coverage table with one row for every item of the method.
entries.number: Each program passes its JavaScript hook's own test file (134, 48, 42, 27, 23, 10 and 8 cases); the set-up 58 tests; the clean-clone check passes every line on Windows; the coverage table holds 280 rows, none without a mark
entries.gain: one hook call 2.8 to 6.8 times faster than through its JavaScript hook (median of 20, one PC); no gain on tokens or quality measured

entries.name: Kit mode in the JavaScript hooks, and their tests run against either form
entries.what: Started with --harness-kit a hook keeps state, briefs, widths and logs under the project it is given, so it holds sessions in a repository other than this one; without the argument it behaves as before. The hooks' test files run against the JavaScript hook or, with KIT_HOOK_BIN_DIR, against its Rust program. A test file of its own for the tier hook.
entries.number: Test files pass both ways: window-ceiling 134, fanout-gate 48, creep-gate 42, count-gate 27 with 2 skipped in a clean clone, tier hook 24

entries.name: The queue: a process group off Windows, a folder and a slot count by option
entries.what: Off Windows a timed-out command's whole process group is stopped, not only its direct child; a project can give the queue a folder of its own, read or set the number of slots, and lift the timeout ceiling for one call. On Windows with no new option it behaves as before.
entries.number: The landing script's 7 tests and the parallel commands' 6 tests pass against it
